items.title: Frank Capp interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: It was so much fun playing with him... I did a tour with Sweets and Buck Clayton in Europe. It was called “The Count’s Men”... I played the drums

ctx.x: Well we spoke with them yesterday and it was marvelous.

Oh you talked with them? That must have been great. I mean Sweets has got some of the funniest expressions — I doubt whether he used them all — but you know like some of those Southern colloquialisms you call them. Like, “He’s tighter than a chicken’s instep.” You know that kind of thing. Or, “He’s so cheap he’s got enough money to air condition a cotton field.
One of the guys said, “If he looked any sharper I’d be bleeding.”

items.title: Frank Capp interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I did a set with Sweets last night

ctx.x: Oh, I’m sorry. I thought my watch was slow. We’ve had some great conversations with people trying to figure out what was it that made the Basie band swing like it did.

Well I mean there could be a lot of theories. But first of all I think it comes from the leader. I mean Count Basie had a great, great sense of time. He was a swinging piano player. He could hit two notes and you could feel the swing. I think maybe that’s where it stems. Secondly, he had great arrangements, or maybe that’s thirdly. Maybe secondly is the men. Because he had great swinging players. He had the cream of the crop back in the 40s. I mean you couldn’t, every band in the country at that time idolized the…
Well we spoke with them yesterday and it was marvelous.
